claims.claim: Nebius announced a five-year Meta AI-infrastructure agreement with $12B of dedicated capacity plus up to $15B of additional available compute capacity, with delivery beginning in early 2027.

factors.name: contracted AI infrastructure demand
factors.basis: large long-duration hyperscaler commitments materially improve forward demand visibility

risks.risk: Large contracted commitments require substantial timely capacity buildout and create customer concentration/execution exposure.

causalEdges.mechanism: long-term offtake supports financing and deployment of AI factories
causalEdges.falsifier: capacity delivery slips materially or contracted customers reduce/terminate commitments

unknowns.unknown: Exact margin and return profile of the large Meta capacity commitments is not established by this source.

claims.claim: Nebius raised approximately $775M in senior secured debt backed by GPU infrastructure and contracted cash flows; the company said the facility plus customer cash flows covers more than 100% of capex for the underlying deployment.

factors.name: capital execution
factors.basis: asset-backed financing tied to contracted cash flows reduces equity-only funding dependence for a deployment

risks.risk: Rapid infrastructure scaling remains capital intensive and leverage increases fixed obligations.

causalEdges.mechanism: secured financing funds GPU infrastructure against contracted economics
causalEdges.falsifier: financing costs rise or deployment economics fail to cover obligations

unknowns.unknown: No canonical valuation conclusion is asserted.
